topic.subject: physics
topic.title: Speed-time graphs and describing motion
topic.scopeBasis: TGS 2025-26 Newton's Laws and Applying Forces; TGS 2026-27 speed-time graphs
topic.overview: A speed-time graph is a compact story of motion. Its height gives speed and its slope shows how quickly speed changes.
learningGoals: Recall the precise Year 8 scientific vocabulary and symbols.
Apply the idea to an unfamiliar example rather than relying on recognition.
Use the command word, show working where needed and include every mark point.
mustMemoriseRules: Time belongs on the x-axis and speed on the y-axis.
A horizontal line above zero shows constant speed.
A line on zero shows the object is stationary.
An upward slope shows acceleration and a downward slope shows deceleration.
A steeper slope represents a greater rate of change of speed when scales are the same.
A vertical line would imply an instantaneous speed change and is usually not physically realistic.
Calculate average speed from total distance divided by total time when distance data are supplied.

mustMemoriseVocabulary.meaning: a graph showing how speed changes with time
speed that does not change with time
increase in velocity per unit time
decrease in speed per unit time
change in vertical quantity divided by change in horizontal quantity
one section of a graph representing a stage of motion
total distance divided by total time

workedExamples.prompt: A graph rises from 0 to 12 m/s, stays horizontal, then slopes to zero. Describe.
workedExamples.answer: The object accelerates, travels at constant speed, then decelerates to rest.

workedExamples.prompt: A journey covers 750 m in 60 s. Calculate average speed.

practicals.title: Create motion data
practicals.aim: Produce data for an object's speed over time.
practicals.variables: IV: time; DV: speed; controls depend on route/object when comparing trials.
practicals.method: Use a motion sensor or light gates, record speed at equal time intervals, plot time on x and speed on y, then describe each segment.
practicals.expectedResult: Different stages show rising, horizontal or falling sections.
practicals.safety: Keep the track clear, use a safe speed and stop equipment before it leaves the runway.
practicals.evaluation: Use automatic sensors to reduce reaction-time error, repeat the motion pattern and use sensible scales.

commonMistakes: Treating a horizontal speed-time line as stationary even when it is above zero.
examTips: Read one segment at a time.
Say what happens to speed, not merely 'the line goes up'.
Check axis scales before comparing steepness.
beforeStartingPractice: Read the key rules once, cover them, then retrieve them aloud or in writing.
Use MC first for confidence, but finish with typed, calculation, practical or explanation evidence.
After an error, study the explanation; the same concept returns later in a different format and again after 2 and 7 days.

practicals.subject: physics
practicals.title: Create motion data
practicals.aim: Produce data for an object's speed over time.
practicals.variables: IV: time; DV: speed; controls depend on route/object when comparing trials.
practicals.method: Use a motion sensor or light gates, record speed at equal time intervals, plot time on x and speed on y, then describe each segment.
practicals.expectedResult: Different stages show rising, horizontal or falling sections.
practicals.safety: Keep the track clear, use a safe speed and stop equipment before it leaves the runway.
practicals.evaluation: Use automatic sensors to reduce reaction-time error, repeat the motion pattern and use sensible scales.
